opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full_time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed. Max for full_time without owning role is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin to Source Code, which exceeds max of read. Recommend read.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer; her role is Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed under either interpretation. However, the two notes conflict on employment type: HR reports full_time (max write for a non-owning role), while Security reports contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training for contractors). Admin exceeds both maxima. Granting read is the highest level that is valid under both notes and is therefore the safe/appropriate grant.
